newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CORPORATE BONDS -- High-yield issuance strong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CORPORATE BONDS -- High-yield issuance strong.

text.p: Flourishing new high-yield issues captured all attention on Thursday, with several deals upsized and trading higher in secondary markets, dealers said.
Meanwhile, solid bids for investment grade corporate bonds pushed spreads marginally tighter on Thursday as long U.S. Treasury yields rose, dealers said.

Leading high-yield issuance, Integrated Health Services issued $450 million 9-1/2 percent 10-year B1/single-B senior subordinated notes via Smith Barney Inc. The deal, which was increased in size by $200 million, was quoted up 1-1/2 points from its initial offered level near the close.

Elsewhere, Stone Container's planned offering of $250 million in units was upsized to $275 million before pricing at a final yield of 12.25 percent, according to lead manager Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette. The B3/B-minus units consist of 10-3/4 percent senior subordinated debentures and 1-1/2 percent supplemental interest certificates.
The offering is part of a $700 million funding program announced by Stone last week. Stone said the plan will meet its financing and debt amortization needs and restore appropriate liquidity.
Also upsized and priced was Chief Auto Parts Inc's $130 million 10-1/2 percent B2/single-B eight year senior notes, priced through lead manager Credit Suisse First Boston.
Finally, Navistar Financial Corp sold $100 million 9 percent B1/B-plus five-year debt at par via a J.P. Morgan Securities syndicate.

Traders noted pricings were rapidly becoming richer after the April correction, and, in some cases, tighter than they would have been at market highs in February. Some buysiders, in fact, have forecast new issue spreads will start leveling out in the near-term.

Turning to high-grades, traders said industrial debt prices were strongly bid as evidenced by more tigthening in Norfolk Southern Corp and CSX Corp railroad debt. Spreads in general were two to three basis points tighter on the week, they added, due primarily to dealers beefing up inventories.

Treasury securties headed lower for the second consecutive session dominated by hedge fund selling, analysts said. In addition, lackluster trading ahead of the long U.S. Memorial Day holiday weekend was blamed for a drift in prices.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended an early close of 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on Friday and a full close on Monday in observance of the holiday.
The benchmark 30-year bond closed down 11/32 at 95-14/32 to yield 6.99 percent. The 10-year T-note closed down 5/32 at 99-3/32 to yield 6.75 percent.
